payload.featureSpecification:
External Notification Channels & Subscription Rules

Extend the existing In-App Notification & Activity Feed System with outbound delivery channels (Slack, Discord, browser push) and fine-grained per-project subscription rules. Reuse the existing notification event records, per-user preference model, and quiet-hours logic.

1. Channel connections
- A workspace admin can connect a Slack incoming webhook, a Discord webhook, or browser push.
- Connections are stored per workspace with display name, channel type, webhook URL (encrypted at rest), and enabled flag.
- Admins can test a connection (send a sample message), disable it, or delete it.
- Browser push uses the standard Web Push flow: per-device subscription registration, public key exposure, and stale-subscription cleanup on delivery failure.

2. Delivery routing
- Each notification type can be routed to any combination of channels, configured per workspace by admins.
- Outbound delivery reuses the existing notification event records: a routing step decides which channel deliveries to enqueue.
- Deliveries are queued and retried up to 3 times with backoff; permanently failed deliveries are recorded with the failure reason.
- Quiet hours from the existing preference model apply to browser push; Slack/Discord are workspace-level.

3. Message formatting
- Slack/Discord messages render actor, action, target entity title, project name, and a deep link back into the app.
- Status changes show old to new status; due-date warnings show the due date; agent run completions show outcome.
- Batched events render as one message with an occurrence count.

4. Subscription rules per project
- A user can follow or mute individual projects: muted projects send nothing to any channel, followed projects bypass type-level off for in-app notifications.
- A user can follow a single work item to receive all events on it and its children.
- Following/muting is exposed on the project page and the work item detail view.

5. Admin & settings UI
- Workspace settings: channel connection list with add/test/disable/delete, and a routing matrix (notification type by channel).
- User settings: browser push opt-in per device, project follow/mute list, followed work items list.
- A log view of the last 50 failed deliveries with reason and retry status.

6. Quality
- Unit tests for routing decisions, retry/backoff, quiet-hours interaction with push, and follow/mute precedence.
- E2E test: connect a webhook, assign a work item, message delivered with correct deep link; mute project, no message.
- Webhook calls must never block the originating mutation; deliveries are strictly asynchronous.
- Document channel setup, the routing matrix, and follow/mute precedence.
